speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, I'm Connie Loizis.
zh: 你好，我是 Connie Loizis。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Alex Gove.
zh: 这位是 Alex Gove。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is Strictly VC Download.
zh: 这里是 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, and welcome back to Strictly VC Download.
zh: 你好，欢迎回到 Strictly VC Download。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our guest this week is Vijay Pandey.
zh: 我们本周的嘉宾是 Vijay Pandey。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pandey started as a theoretical physicist, nabbing a PhD from MIT before landing at Stanford in 1999, where he built something called Folding at Home, turning millions of home computers into a supercomputer for disease research.
zh: Pandey 最初是一名理论物理学家，在 MIT 拿到博士学位后，于 1999 年来到 Stanford，在那里他建立了名为 Folding at Home 的项目，把数百万台家用电脑变成一台用于疾病研究的超级计算机。

speaker: Unknown
en: In 2014, he talked his way into Andreessen Horowitz, convincing the firm to bet on healthcare and life sciences, a category it had explicitly ruled out, and built it into a nearly $4 billion practice.
zh: 2014 年，他凭口才进入了 Andreessen Horowitz，说服这家公司押注医疗健康和生命科学——这是该公司当时明确排除的领域——并把它打造成了一个规模接近 40 亿美元的业务。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then, a little more than a year ago, he walked away to build something smaller.
zh: 然后，大约一年多以前，他离开去创建一个更小的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: His new firm, VZVC, co-founded with longtime investor Zach Werner.
zh: 他的新公司 VZVC，与资深投资人 Zach Werner 联合创立。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is a deliberate bet against bigness, you could say.
zh: 可以说，这是对“做大”的一次刻意反向押注。

speaker: Unknown
en: It intends to make not dozens of investments from its new fund, but only a handful.
zh: 这家公司打算用新基金做的不是几十笔投资，而只是寥寥几笔。

speaker: Unknown
en: It also doesn't feature associates or other layers.
zh: 它也不设 associate 或其他层级。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the two are building it from scratch, and because it's AI native, it's an interesting example of what more VC firms could look like in the future.
zh: 因为两人是从零开始搭建，而且它是 AI native 的，所以它是未来更多 VC 公司可能的样子一个有趣的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: In addition to the mechanics of the firm, we get into why he's betting concentration beats breadth right now.
zh: 除了公司的运作机制，我们还聊到了为什么他现在押注集中胜过分散。

speaker: Unknown
en: How a VC writing checks into buzzy biotech startups that are growing quickly thinks about how much money to put to work.
zh: 一位向高速增长的热门生物科技初创公司开出支票的 VC，是如何思考该投入多少钱的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we also touch on a challenge that's central to the intersection of AI and biotech, which is that you can't scrape biology off of the internet the way you can scrape text.
zh: 我们还触及了一个处于 AI 与生物科技交汇点核心的挑战，那就是你无法像抓取文本那样从互联网上抓取生物学数据。

speaker: Unknown
en: Every company has to generate its own data to a certain degree, but that means every model is trained on its own silo.
zh: 每家公司都在一定程度上必须自己生成数据，但这意味着每个模型都是在自己的数据孤岛上训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Raising the obvious question, is that fragmenting the field's collective progress
zh: 由此引出一个明显的问题：这是否正在割裂该领域的集体进步？

speaker: Unknown
en: Or is there a real path toward biology's version of open source AI?
zh: 还是说，确实存在一条通向生物科技版开源 AI 的现实路径？

speaker: Unknown
en: Vijay's got strong opinions on both.
zh: Vijay 对这两点都有强烈的观点。

speaker: Unknown
en: It had been a long time since we'd caught up with Pondy, who is well-known in Silicon Valley circles through his time at Stanford and through Andreessen Horowitz.
zh: 我们已经很久没和 Pondy 联系了，他因在 Stanford 和 Andreessen Horowitz 的经历而在硅谷圈子里广为人知。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was really great to talk with him.
zh: 和他交谈真的非常愉快。

speaker: Unknown
en: We hope that you will enjoy and learn from this chat too, and we will see you back here next week.
zh: 我们希望你们也能从这次对话中享受并学到东西，我们下周再见。

speaker: Unknown
en: Vijay, it's really great to be reconnecting with you again.
zh: Vijay，能再次和你重新联系真是太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I cannot believe it's been quite so long.
zh: 我不敢相信已经过去了这么长时间。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations on your new firm.
zh: 祝贺你的新公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: For people who've seen your name, know that you were leading Andreessen Horowitz's biotech effort for many years, but maybe don't really know your background, can you just kind of give us the skinny?
zh: 对于那些见过你的名字、知道你多年来领导 Andreessen Horowitz 生物科技业务、但不太了解你背景的人，你能简单介绍一下吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: You started off, I think, as a physicist before winding up in biology.
zh: 我记得你最初是物理学家，后来才进入生物学领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, absolutely.
zh: 对，没问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's a fun question.
zh: 这是个有趣的问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So actually, I was in my first startup when I was 15 years old.
zh: 实际上，我 15 岁时就创办了我的第一家初创公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh, wow.
zh: 哦，哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it was me with my friends, Andy Gavin and Jason Rubin, building Naughty Dog Software, a computer gaming company.
zh: 那是我和我的朋友 Andy Gavin 和 Jason Rubin 一起，创建了 Naughty Dog Software，一家电脑游戏公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: It was such a great education to do that at a young age, where we were writing software that shipped on Sega Genesis and so on, but doing it basically three of us with Electronic Arts as our studio.
zh: 在那么小的年纪做这件事是一次极好的教育，我们编写的软件发行在 Sega Genesis 等平台上，但基本上就是我们三个人，以 Electronic Arts 作为我们的工作室。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think I fell in love with startups in that moment, but also...
zh: 我觉得就是在那一刻我爱上了初创公司，同时也……

speaker: Unknown
en: I went to college and grad school.
zh: 我去上了大学和研究生院。

speaker: Unknown
en: My degrees, as you mentioned, are in theoretical physics.
zh: 正如你提到的，我的学位是理论物理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I got a PhD in theoretical physics from MIT.
zh: 所以我在 MIT 拿到了理论物理博士学位。

speaker: Unknown
en: And, you know, you might think like, well, what does that have to do with anything today?
zh: 而且，你知道，你可能会想：这和今天的事有什么关系呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of the biggest conveniences of my career is that all the math and a lot of the, even the intuition from AI is a lot of the same math from theoretical physics, especially condensed matter physics.
zh: 我觉得我职业生涯中最大的幸运之一是，AI 所用的所有数学，甚至很多直觉，和理论物理的数学是同一套，尤其是凝聚态物理。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I've been working on neural nets even when I was in college.
zh: 所以我甚至在大学时就在研究神经网络。

speaker: Unknown
en: But at that time, biology was a really big thing.
zh: 但在那个年代，生物学是一件非常大的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: You might remember the Human Genome Project.
zh: 你可能还记得人类基因组计划。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so there's a lot of excitement behind that.
zh: 那背后有很多令人兴奋的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that really pulled me from physics to biology.
zh: 所以这真的把我从物理拉向了生物。

speaker: Unknown
en: And combining those two loves of biology and startups, I wanted to be a professor at Stanford.
zh: 出于对生物学和初创公司这两份热爱的结合，我想成为 Stanford 的教授。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so I started there in 1999.
zh: 于是我 1999 年在那里入职。

speaker: Unknown
en: And pretty quickly, like people from Sandhill, VCs from Sandhill contacted me to help them with diligence and to contact the advisory boards and board directors of companies.
zh: 很快，Sand Hill 的这些人、Sand Hill 的 VC 联系上我，帮他们做尽调，并联系各公司的顾问委员会和董事会成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that was just such a joy for me as I was like back in that ecosystem and so on.
zh: 那对我来说简直是莫大的乐趣，因为我重新回到了那个生态系统等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most notably, I built Folding at Home, the large scale supercomputer project, which basically allowed us to preview a lot of the issues that we now see in AI, especially the bitter lesson that compute is such a big deal.
zh: 最值得一提的是，我创建了 Folding at Home 这个大规模超级计算机项目，它基本上让我们预览到了如今在 AI 中看到的许多问题，尤其是“苦涩的教训”——算力如此重要这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Before you go on, I just would love to index for a minute on Folding at Home, because I do think it's really interesting, and I don't know that this broader readership or listenership is going to know it.
zh: 在你继续之前，我想花一分钟聚焦一下 Folding at Home,因为我确实觉得它非常有意思，而且我不确定更广泛的读者或听众是否了解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, yeah.
zh: 是的，是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So to set the context, and we found in 2000, it's something that's actually still going on strong.
zh: 先交代一下背景，我们是 2000 年创立的，它实际上至今仍在强劲地进行着。

speaker: Unknown
en: But the idea is that my group at Stanford wrote software that people download and actually shipped natively on the PS3.
zh: 当时的想法是，我在斯坦福的团队编写了一款供人们下载的软件，它甚至原生搭载在 PS3 上发布。

speaker: Unknown
en: And by running that software, your computer became part of this large-scale computer.
zh: 通过运行这款软件，你的计算机就成为这台大规模计算机的一部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we were actually some of the first to even do any sort of compute on GPUs.
zh: 而且我们实际上是最早在 GPU 上进行任何形式计算的人之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so with that, with GPUs and the PS3, we were able to build a very, very powerful machine at a very low cost.
zh: 因此，凭借 GPU 和 PS3,我们能够以极低的成本建造一台非常非常强大的机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So incredible.
zh: 太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So people donating their idle processing power.
zh: 所以人们是在捐赠他们的空闲算力。

speaker: Unknown
en: How many people were involved in this?
zh: 有多少人参与了这件事？

speaker: Unknown
en: How many are involved in it now?
zh: 现在有多少人参与？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I actually don't have the most recent stats, but at a day day, this was like tens of millions of people contributing.
zh: 我实际上没有最新的统计数据，但在高峰期，大约有数千万人参与贡献。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the fun thing especially was that, you know, I think people could really get involved and they could see sort of what their contributions were.
zh: 而且我觉得特别有意思的一点是，你知道，人们可以真正参与进来，并且能看到自己的贡献是什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: But maybe the most poetic way to talk about it is that it was not just a supercomputer, but maybe a little bit of a time machine.
zh: 但要说最有诗意的方式，那就是它不仅仅是一台超级计算机，或许还有点像一台时间机器。

speaker: Unknown
en: That allowed us to do calculations 10 years ago or 15 years ago that now are becoming routine.
zh: 它让我们在 10 年前或 15 年前就能进行如今已成为常规操作的计算。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that sort of allowed us to have a lot of creativity and sort of try out things.
zh: 而这在一定程度上让我们拥有了大量的创造力，可以尝试各种东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Phenomenal.
zh: 太棒了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there you are at Stanford teaching, I guess, biophysics and involved in this or no?
zh: 所以当时你在斯坦福任教，我猜是生物物理学，并且参与这个项目吗？还是没参与？

speaker: Unknown
en: Primarily chemistry.
zh: 主要是化学。

speaker: Unknown
en: But, you know, like the thing about professors is we mostly run a research lab and teaching is the thing that we do to pay the bills and so on.
zh: 但是，你知道，教授这回事是，我们主要是运营一个研究实验室，教书是我们用来支付账单之类的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And how did you land at Andreessen Horwitz?
zh: 那你是怎么来到 Andreessen Horowitz 的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So in 2014, I met Mark and Ben, you know, Mark and Andreessen and Ben Horwitz, and we had a mutual friend and a business partner, Balaji Shrinivasan, who had worked with me in a couple of different capacities and was actually even briefly at my Stanford lab.
zh: 在 2014 年，我认识了 Mark 和 Ben,你知道，Mark Andreessen 和 Ben Horowitz,我们有一个共同的朋友兼商业伙伴 Balaji Shrinivasan,他曾以几种不同的身份与我共事，甚至还在我的斯坦福实验室短暂待过。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Balaji introduced us, you know, we really hit it off.
zh: 于是 Balaji 引荐了我们，你知道，我们一见如故。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think we saw a lot of things very similarly in terms of the future of technology.
zh: 我觉得在对技术未来的看法上，我们的很多观点都非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: It seems like that required a lot of forethought because I feel like even in 2014, it was like just not something a lot of VCs were keen to dive into.
zh: 这似乎需要很多先见之明，因为我觉得即使在 2014 年，很多风险投资家也不太热衷于投入这个领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know that you've said that biology is moving from science of discovery to something you can engineer.
zh: 我知道你说过，生物学正在从一门发现科学转变为一门可以工程化的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: What does that mean in practice?
zh: 这在实践中意味着什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: Even amongst many biologists today, there's a sense that biology is so complicated, there is no way that a human being could understand it.
zh: 即使在今天，很多生物学家也有一种感觉，认为生物学太复杂了，人类不可能理解它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that actually may be true in many ways, but I think what's shifted is that AI and machine learning allows computers to wrap their type of understanding on something very, very complicated.
zh: 而我认为这在很多方面可能确实是真的，但我认为已经改变的是，AI 和机器学习让计算机能够对非常非常复杂的事物形成它们那种类型的理解。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's, I think, this AI machine learning shift that has allowed something that really wasn't possible before.
zh: 我认为正是这场 AI 机器学习的转变，让以前真正不可能的事情成为可能。

speaker: Unknown
en: Either to understand biology, which is to try to figure out what targets you want your drugs to hit for specific diseases, to be able to make those drugs, and now even to help in the clinical trials, which are the most expensive part of the process.
zh: 无论是理解生物学——也就是尝试弄清楚你希望药物针对特定疾病命中哪些靶点——还是制造这些药物，现在甚至可以帮助临床试验，而临床试验是这个过程中最昂贵的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're shifting from pure discovery to something that is very much engineering, although it's engineering in a biological context.
zh: 所以你正在从纯粹的发现转向非常工程化的东西，尽管它是在生物学语境下的工程。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when you talk about the clinical trials, you mean because so much of it can be done synthetically right now, so not as many people need to be roped into the process?
zh: 当你谈到临床试验时，你是指因为现在很多东西都可以合成完成了，所以不需要那么多人被拉进这个流程？

speaker: Unknown
en: That's, I think, very much an aspiration.
zh: 那我认为在很大程度上还是一种愿景。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the big thing right now is that the biggest cost for drugs is the cost of clinical trials.
zh: 我认为现在最重要的一点是，药物最大的成本就是临床试验的成本。

speaker: Unknown
en: The cost and time to get to clinical trials has been shrinking, and especially with AI, but it could still cost like hundreds of millions of dollars to run a trial.
zh: 进入临床试验的成本和时间一直在缩短，尤其是在 AI 的加持下，但运行一项试验仍然可能花费数亿美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the end reason why drugs are very expensive is that the probability of a drug going from the first trial to the end of the third, the probability of a success is just 20%.
zh: 而药物非常昂贵的根本原因在于，一种药从第一次试验走到第三期试验结束，成功的概率只有 20%。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, 8 out of 10 fail.
zh: 你知道，10 个里有 8 个会失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so you can imagine if these things cost hundreds of millions of dollars and like most of them fail, the amortized cost of drugs gets really, really high.
zh: 所以你可以想象，如果这些东西每个要花费数亿美元，而且大多数都会失败，那么药物的分摊成本就会变得非常非常高。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think the lesson here is that the reason why they fail typically is not that the biologist did something wrong or did something poor.
zh: 我觉得这里的教训是，它们失败的原因通常不是生物学家做错了什么或做得不好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's that all the experiments that these drugs were designed on were on animal models like mice and other animals.
zh: 而是这些药物所依据的所有实验都是在小鼠等动物模型上进行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: In the end, these animal models are just not very predictive of humans.
zh: 归根结底，这些动物模型对人类的预测性并不强。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think where AI really changes this is that while it would be unethical to do experiments on human beings the way you would do on mice, the ability to take human data
zh: 而我认为 AI 真正改变这一点的地方在于，虽然像在小鼠身上那样在人类身上做实验是不道德的，但获取人类数据

speaker: Unknown
en: And bring it together in a model is something AI actually is really very well suited for.
zh: 并将其整合到一个模型中，这正是 AI 真正非常擅长的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: This AI model is not going to be perfect, but that is going to be way better than any animal model would be.
zh: 这个 AI 模型不会是完美的，但它会比任何动物模型都好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: Once it crosses that bar, that's where it gets really exciting.
zh: 一旦跨过那个门槛，事情就真正令人兴奋了。

speaker: Unknown
en: But beyond that, you and I care not just about does the drug get approved, but let's say if you or I were sick or one of our loved ones was sick, like, would that work for us?
zh: 但除此之外，你和我关心的不仅仅是药物能否获批，而是假设你或我生病了，或者我们的某个亲人病了，它对我们有效吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And where this starts to transition now into is even not just in helping design drugs, but now onto the other side, being a doctor and seeing, well, actually, is this drug the right drug for me?
zh: 而这现在开始过渡到的方向，甚至不仅仅是帮助设计药物，而是转到另一端，成为一名医生，然后去看，实际上，这药是不是适合我的药？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's something that actually also itself can be life or death.
zh: 而这件事本身实际上也可以是生死攸关的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you, I guess, elaborate a little bit more?
zh: 你能,我想,再多展开讲一点吗?

speaker: Unknown
en: You're talking about the ability to personalize medicine?
zh: 你说的是个性化医疗的能力?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, I think the jargon here is so-called precision medicine.
zh: 是的,我认为这里的行话叫所谓的精准医疗。

speaker: Unknown
en: If you've ever gone to a doctor with something not trivial, there's only so much they can tell.
zh: 如果你曾经因为某个不算轻微的问题去看医生,他们能告诉你的东西其实很有限。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then they give you a drug.
zh: 然后他们会给你开一种药。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if sometimes that works, but sometimes it doesn't, they give you another drug, then another drug.
zh: 有时那个药有效,但有时无效,他们再给你开另一种药,然后再换一种。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this happens in cancer.
zh: 这种情况发生在癌症中。

speaker: Unknown
en: It happens in lots of different areas.
zh: 也发生在许多不同的领域。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we would all be much better off if the first drug was the right one.
zh: 如果第一种药就是对的,我们所有人都会好得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is very much a data problem.
zh: 这在很大程度上是一个数据问题。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's the data of
zh: 它是关于……的数据

speaker: Unknown
en: Reading your blood tests and understanding all the nuances and then understanding how you may be similar or different to other people.
zh: 读取你的血液检测报告,理解所有细微差异,然后理解你可能与其他人有哪些相似或不同之处。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of the big transitions we're seeing in healthcare right now is that when you get blood tests, typically your values are compared to population averages, but really they should be compared to like, well, is this weird for you?
zh: 我们现在在医疗领域看到的一个重大转变是,当你做血液检测时,通常你的数值是和人群平均值做比较的,但实际上应该是和这样的问题做比较:这对你来说是否异常?

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we're starting to do also on the medicine side is to be able to just understand what would be right for the individual.
zh: 而我们在药物这一侧也开始做的,就是能够理解什么对个体才是对的。

en: So I think that part is very exciting.
zh: 所以我认为那一部分是非常令人兴奋的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think if I were to pick the one thing that I've really tried to think about that I wish I knew in the beginning, and I think it took me some time to really appreciate is that as seductive as the coolest technologies are, it really always comes back down to the good market.
zh: 我认为如果要我挑出一件我真正努力思考过、希望一开始就知道的事情——而且我认为花了我一些时间才真正领会——那就是，无论最酷的技术多么诱人，归根结底总是要回到好的市场。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I tell my founders is like,
zh: 我告诉我的创始人是这样的，

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially the ones that are coming from the science or the product side, for them to take all their brilliance and creativity and really apply it to the going market side.
zh: 尤其是那些来自科学或产品一侧的人，让他们把自己所有的才华和创造力真正应用到进入市场那一侧。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that the go-to-market part is at least as hard or harder than the technology side.
zh: 而进入市场这部分，至少和技术那部分一样难，或者更难。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so a lot of my investments in the last few years
zh: 所以我过去几年的很多投资，

speaker: Unknown
en: The ones where the go-to-market actually is really clever.
zh: 那些进入市场实际上非常聪明的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think about function health as being a great example where this direct-to-consumer, which is, by the way, a lot of people would say direct-to-consumer health would never work.
zh: 所以我想到了 Function Health，把它当作一个很好的例子，这种直接面向消费者的模式——顺便说一句，很多人会说直接面向消费者的健康永远不会成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: They are very much proving that that's not the case.
zh: 他们正在非常有力地证明情况并非如此。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think Jonathan Squirtland there, the CEO and co-founder, he really thinks about go-to-market first and foremost, and then picks the technologies to do what he needs to do to get that done.
zh: 我认为 Jonathan Squirtland，那里的 CEO 兼联合创始人，他真的把进入市场放在最首要的位置来思考，然后再挑选技术来完成他需要做的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think in our world, especially for what the possibilities are now, I think that's actually one thing I wish I thought about from the beginning.
zh: 所以我认为在我们的世界里，尤其是对现在存在的种种可能性而言，我觉得这确实是我希望一开始就想到的一件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's interesting.
zh: 这很有意思。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't know anything about Function Health, so can you talk a little bit about the product and what is so special about its go-to-market?
zh: 我对 Function Health 一无所知，所以你能稍微谈谈这个产品，以及它的进入市场策略有什么特别之处吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so I think the goal for Function Health is to give you agency over your health.
zh: 是的，我认为 Function Health 的目标是让你对自己的健康拥有主观能动性。

speaker: Unknown
en: You join as a member, and twice a year, every six months, you get your blood tested, and then it's a huge panel of tests that, if you try to get it from your doctor, it costs probably about $5,000, the way the medical system is set up.
zh: 你作为会员加入，一年两次，每六个月，你做一次血液检测，然后那是一大套检测项目，如果你试图从医生那里得到它，按医疗体系的设置方式，大概要花 5000 美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: And originally Function was $500, and now it's actually like $365, so like a dollar a day.
zh: 最初 Function 是 500 美元，现在实际上大约是 365 美元，就像一天一美元。

speaker: Unknown
en: The idea is from these blood tests, you actually can see where you are today and what are the specific things that you'd want to do differently.
zh: 这个想法是，从这些血液检测中，你实际上可以看到你今天的状况，以及你想要做出哪些具体的不同做法。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've layered in since series A multiple acquisitions, including Ezra.
zh: 自 A 轮以来，他们叠加了多次收购，包括 Ezra。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ezra is basically the function analog for imaging, so MRI and CT.
zh: Ezra 基本上是功能对应于成像的版本，也就是 MRI 和 CT。

speaker: Unknown
en: Imaging is like you might get a blood test and say, well, okay, now we want to know more, so the next step would be imaging.
zh: 成像是这样的：你可能做了一次血液检测，然后说，好吧，现在我们想知道更多，所以下一步就是成像。

speaker: Unknown
en: They've done acquisitions into supplements and into phlebotomy and in a sense are building up a consumer-focused preventive healthcare system.
zh: 他们进行了针对补充剂和抽血服务的收购，在某种意义上正在构建一个以消费者为中心的预防性医疗保健系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think one of the biggest shifts in healthcare that was just starting is the shift from what is in the industry called sick care, where companies make money off of you when you're sick, to prevention, where you make money when they keep you healthy.
zh: 而我认为医疗保健领域刚开始发生的最大转变之一，就是从行业内所说的病患护理（即公司在你生病时从你身上赚钱）转向预防（即当他们让你保持健康时才赚钱）。

speaker: Unknown
en: From the point of view of a patient, you don't want to be sick.
zh: 从病人的角度来看，你不想生病。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's real power in living a capitalist world.
zh: 而且在一个资本主义世界里生活确实有其真实的力量。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in a capitalist world where people make money from you being sick, there'll be a lot of incentives for you to be sick.
zh: 但在一个人们从你生病中赚钱的资本主义世界里，会有很多让你生病的激励。

speaker: Unknown
en: If instead things were aligned such that companies made money by keeping you healthy,
zh: 如果相反，各种事物被调整成公司通过让你保持健康来赚钱，

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something where now finally these financial incentives are aligned with what you and I want.
zh: 那就是现在这些财务激励终于和你我所想要的保持一致的地方。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so Function is a good example that Devoted Health is another really good example of where these incentives have been aligned.
zh: 所以 Function 是一个很好的例子，Devoted Health 是另一个激励被对齐的非常好的例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: Devoted is like Medicare Advantage Company, so it's for seniors.
zh: Devoted 是一家类似 Medicare Advantage 的公司，所以它是面向老年人的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Function is direct to consumer.
zh: Function 是直接面向消费者的。

speaker: Unknown
en: But in either case, there is this alignment between who's paying for it and wanting to keep you healthy.
zh: 但无论哪种情况，付款方和希望让你保持健康这两者之间都存在这种一致性。

speaker: Unknown
en: How focused are you on D2C versus otherwise enterprise?
zh: 你对 D2C 相对于企业端有多专注？

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the thing about the healthcare system right now, typically the customer is the insurance company, not the patient.
zh: 所以我认为现在的医疗体系，通常客户是保险公司，而不是病人。

speaker: Unknown
en: In direct-to-consumer, that's something where the customer and the patient are the same.
zh: 在直接面向消费者的模式中，客户和病人是同一个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think there's been a lot of tailwinds post-COVID where, you know, COVID obviously was a big ordeal for all of us.
zh: 而且我认为 COVID 之后有很多顺风，你知道，COVID 显然对我们所有人都是一大考验。

speaker: Unknown
en: And people started thinking about like, well, I want to understand my health myself.
zh: 人们开始想，嗯，我想自己了解自己的健康。

speaker: Unknown
en: I want to be not just like a product of the system, but I want to be someone actually involved with real agency in it.
zh: 我不想只是这个系统的产物，而是想成为一个真正参与其中、拥有真正主观能动性的人。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think people are realizing that that's something that now actually is doable with tools like Function.
zh: 我认为人们正在意识到，借助像 Function 这样的工具，这在现在实际上是可行的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on top of that, AI is a natural companion for this.
zh: 除此之外，AI 是这方面的天然伴侣。

speaker: Unknown
en: Obviously, one has to be careful with employing AI yourself, and I'm not suggesting people talk to themselves or anything like that.
zh: 显然，自己使用 AI 时必须小心，我并不是建议人们自言自语或类似的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: But like, I think just the ability, if nothing else, to get data on your own and to know what questions you want to ask your doctor.
zh: 但我认为，哪怕只是能够自己获取数据、知道自己想问医生什么问题，

speaker: Unknown
en: And to be almost like a peer in the room rather than just the subject is a huge advance.
zh: 并且在诊室里几乎像一个平等的对话者而不仅仅是被检查的对象，就是一个巨大的进步。

speaker: Unknown
en: Absolutely.
zh: 完全正确。

speaker: Unknown
en: You don't want to over-rely on these chatbots, but Claude has, in a couple of cases, helped me go to the doctor and say, I think this is this thing and it's turned out to be true.
zh: 你不想过度依赖这些聊天机器人，但 Claude 在好几个情况下帮助我去找医生说，我认为这是这个东西，而结果证明是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I've talked to other people who've used it as another opinion in concert with the actual medical professionals and it's been really helpful.
zh: 我和其他人聊过，他们把它当作与真正的医疗专业人士配合的另一种意见来使用，这真的很有帮助。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's incredible.
zh: 这太不可思议了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, Vijay, help me understand how you are approaching the design of this new firm.
zh: 另外，Vijay，帮我们理解一下你如何设计这家新公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you grew the biotech arm at Anderson Horowitz.
zh: 你在 Anderson Horowitz 培育了生物科技部门。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're managing, I don't know, like two billion-ish altogether?
zh: 你管理的，我不确定，总共大概 20 亿美元左右？

speaker: Unknown
en: No, I knew at the end almost four.
zh: 不，我知道到最后差不多 40 亿。

speaker: Unknown
en: Oh my gosh.
zh: 哦天哪。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Wow.
zh: 哇。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you're now targeting what, like 400 million?
zh: 那你现在目标是多少，4 亿美元左右？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So right now we're doing something really quite different.
zh: 所以现在我们做的事情非常不一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: And actually, so Marc Andreessen, when he was talking about the two types of firms that he thought would be successful, he talked about, and I think he's maybe saying this a little tongue in cheek, but he talked about Gucci and Walmart.
zh: 实际上，Marc Andreessen 在谈到他认为会成功的两类公司时，他谈到——我想他可能说这话时带点玩笑——他谈到了 Gucci 和 Walmart。

speaker: Unknown
en: And like, you know, either you run a very small firm or you have a really big one.
zh: 就是说，你要么经营一家非常小的公司，要么拥有一家真正大的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: So A6 and Z is obviously a big firm.
zh: 所以 A6 and Z 显然是一家大公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: VZ right now is named after me, Vijay, and my co-founder, Zach Werner.
zh: VZ 现在是以我，Vijay，和我的联合创始人 Zach Werner 命名的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So he's the Z.
zh: 所以他就是那个 Z。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we're intentionally really quite small.
zh: 而我们是有意做得非常小。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the design aspects was that we would actually be very AI native.
zh: 其中一个设计要点是我们实际上会非常 AI 原生。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's actually borne out really well in that to date, we have on the investment side, really just the two of us.
zh: 这一点实际上得到了很好的印证，因为到目前为止，在投资方面，真的只有我们两个人。

speaker: Unknown
en: We were actually intending on hiring associates, but actually it turned out to be with the agents and the things that we've built up, not to be something that we need to do, at least at the moment.
zh: 我们本来打算招聘分析师，但结果发现，凭借智能体和我们构建起来的那些东西，这不是我们需要做的事情，至少目前不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's allowed us also to go really fast in a way that I think, unless you're doing what we're doing, I don't think you could do.
zh: 这也让我们能够以非常快的速度前进，我认为除非你在做我们正在做的事情，否则你是做不到的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think for a lot of people, the junior people are using AI, but the senior people are working with the junior people.
zh: 我认为对很多人来说，初级员工在使用 AI，但资深员工是在和初级员工一起工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so for us to go all in with something that really is hard to do unless you start from scratch, it's very natural to do that.
zh: 所以对我们来说，全力以赴投入一件除非从零开始否则很难做到的事情，是非常自然的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in terms of fundraising, we're still sort of in the fundraise.
zh: 然后在募资方面，我们还在募资过程中。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not going to talk about that, but we have been making investments.
zh: 我不打算谈这个，但我们一直在进行投资。

speaker: Unknown
en: But you're intentionally going a little bit smaller because I'm guessing with your brand and the fact that everybody's very interested in this area, you could probably raise more than what I've read that you're targeting.
zh: 但你是有意做得小一点的，因为我猜凭借你的品牌以及所有人都对这个领域非常感兴趣这一点，你本可以募集到比我读到的你目标金额更多的钱。

speaker: Unknown
en: How do you think about writing checks right now compared to maybe five and 10 years ago?
zh: 你现在写支票(投资)的方式，和五年前、十年前相比，你是怎么考虑的？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so there's two areas that I've been spending most of my time on.
zh: 是的，我大部分时间都花在两个领域上。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is AI for healthcare delivery, which, you know, I did a ton at A16D as well, and then AI for clinical trials.
zh: 一个是医疗交付领域的 AI,这个你知道，我在 A16D 也做过很多，然后是临床试验领域的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: Those are areas that I think are either hot now or are going to become very hot.
zh: 我认为这些领域要么现在很火，要么将会变得非常火。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI for care delivery, a lot of those companies can grow really fast, you know, Function's growing really fast.
zh: 医疗交付领域的 AI,很多这类公司可以增长得非常快，你知道，Function 增长得非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think tech-like growth from these is not unusual, and I think Function's a great exemplar of that.
zh: 所以我认为这类公司有类似科技行业的增长并不罕见，我认为 Function 就是这方面一个很好的范例。

speaker: Unknown
en: The trick, obviously, is that you can't just combine AI willy-nilly as, you know, in anything.
zh: 当然，诀窍在于，你不能随意地把 AI 拼凑进去，就像在任何事情上一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: You have to be able to really understand the healthcare business.
zh: 你必须能够真正理解医疗健康这个行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we look for founders that obviously go very deep in those areas.
zh: 所以我们寻找的创始人显然要在这些领域钻研得很深。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, AI for healthcare delivery is one piece of it.
zh: 所以，医疗交付领域的 AI 是其中一块。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the other is?
zh: 那另一个是？

speaker: Unknown
en: AI for clinical trials.
zh: 临床试验领域的 AI。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, this is the area where...
zh: 那么，这个领域……

speaker: Unknown
en: Let's say right now, like 20% succeed, 80% fail.
zh: 可以说现在，大约 20% 成功，80% 失败。

speaker: Unknown
en: If let's say only 70% failed, you know, which is relatively modest gain.
zh: 假如说只有 70% 失败，你知道，这是相对适度的提升。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm not asking AI to do something heroic.
zh: 我不是要求 AI 做什么英雄般的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means that 30% succeed.
zh: 那就意味着 30% 成功。

speaker: Unknown
en: That means you get 50% more drugs.
zh: 那意味着你能多得到 50% 的药物。

speaker: Unknown
en: The amortized cost of drugs go down by 50%.
zh: 药物的摊销成本下降 50%。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a huge, huge win.
zh: 这是一个巨大的、巨大的胜利。

speaker: Unknown
en: And because this is so tough, you don't need to be a panacea.
zh: 而且因为这件事如此艰难，你不需要成为万灵药。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to just move the needle a bit to be able to actually have a huge impact on the cost, to be able to have huge returns, and actually to be able to change patients' lives.
zh: 你只需要把指针稍微移动一点，就能对成本产生巨大影响，能够带来巨大回报，并且真正能够改变患者的生活。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's great.
zh: 那太好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you give me another, maybe a recent example of a company that fell right into the center of that Venn diagram?
zh: 你能再给我一个例子吗，也许是一个最近正好落在这张韦恩图中心的公司的例子？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we have not made an investment in this space yet and we've been looking and there's many out there doing interesting things.
zh: 好的，我们在这个领域还没有做投资，但我们一直在看，外面有很多在做有趣事情的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: One A6&Z investment is FormationBio, which Ben Liu is a CEO co-founder.
zh: A6&Z 有一笔投资是 FormationBio,CEO 联合创始人是 Ben Liu。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I've seen like tens of companies in this space.
zh: 但我在这个领域见过几十家公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're all taking different approaches.
zh: 它们都在采取不同的方法。

speaker: Unknown
en: But I think one of the things that was striking is that many of them have claims that they can predict whether a drug would work or not with pretty high accuracy.
zh: 但我认为令人印象深刻的一点是，它们中很多都声称，能够以相当高的准确度预测一种药物是否有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's something that would be a fantasy years ago.
zh: 这在几年前还是一种幻想。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's actually I've seen that now in multiple cases.
zh: 而实际上我现在已经在多个案例中看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: That reality is going to change the game quite a bit.
zh: 这个现实将会相当程度上改变局面。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then in terms of the checks, again, has the way that you value a company changed at all?
zh: 那么再回到投资上，你给公司估值的方式有发生变化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: There's two principles we have.
zh: 我们有两个原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: One is that AI really makes the power law more important than ever.
zh: 第一是，AI 确实让幂律变得比以往任何时候都更重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: What I would predict is that the big companies would get really big, that there will be trillion dollar healthcare companies that are built with these types of tools.
zh: 我预测的是，大公司会变得非常大，将会出现用这类工具打造出来的万亿美元医疗健康公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's number one.
zh: 这是第一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then number two is that with AI, though, it doesn't take too much to get to, let's say, 10 million run rate.
zh: 第二点是，不过有了 AI,要达到比如说 1000 万美元的年化收入，并不需要太多。

speaker: Unknown
en: It used to be 10 million run rate was kind of like escape velocity, like, okay, they're going to become a serious company.
zh: 过去 1000 万美元年化收入有点像逃逸速度，就是说，好，他们会成为一家正经的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: But with AI and agents, you can build that pretty fast, but that doesn't mean that it's something that could scale into something really big.
zh: 但有了 AI 和智能体，你可以很快做到那个数字，但这并不意味着它能扩展成真正大的东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so because of that, I think Zach and I have been taking a strategy of either coming in a little later, which would be sort of what some people might call growth, but like maybe or late venture and looking for things where there's, let's say, 30 million run rate.
zh: 因此，我认为 Zach 和我一直采取的策略是，要么稍微晚一点进入，也就是有些人可能所说的成长期投资，或者叫后期风险投资，去寻找那些年化收入比如说达到 3000 万美元的项目。

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, I did the Series A function, but like, you know, they were already around for a while.
zh: 你知道，我投了 Function 的 Series A,但你知道，他们当时已经成立一段时间了。

speaker: Unknown
en: So like, you know, these letters almost sometimes don't mean as much as you might think.
zh: 所以，你知道，这些轮次字母有时候并不像你以为的那么重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So really, I'm looking for a business that's really a scale enough that I could really sort of see the path from here to something really big.
zh: 所以说真的，我找的是业务已经规模化到足够程度、让我能真正看清从现在到成为巨大事物之间路径的公司。

speaker: Unknown
en: Either that or incubations.
zh: 要么就是孵化项目。
